slots.practicalActivity: Install SSDT (SQL Server Data Tools) for Visual Studio if it isn't already installed, then create a new Integration Services project named SSIS_Fundamentals. Open the empty package designer and locate the Control Flow, Data Flow, Parameters, and Event Handlers tabs plus the Connection Managers pane, matching each one to the architecture pieces covered in the lesson.
slots.deliverable: A new SSIS_Fundamentals project open in SSDT containing one renamed, empty package, plus a short written note identifying where Control Flow, Data Flow, and Connection Managers live in the designer and what each is for.

slots.practicalActivity: In the SSIS_Fundamentals project, add an OLE DB Connection Manager pointing at a local SQL Server database, then build your first real package: a single Execute SQL Task that runs a simple SELECT COUNT(*) query against a table in that database. Rename the package descriptively, matching the package/project/solution hierarchy from the lesson.
slots.deliverable: A renamed package containing one OLE DB Connection Manager and one working Execute SQL Task, run successfully in debug mode with the task turning green.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a new package with three Execute SQL Tasks chained in sequence: (1) truncate a staging table, (2) insert a row-count value into a logging table, (3) run a parameterized query. Use the Execute SQL Task's Parameter Mapping and Result Set tabs to capture an output value into a package variable.
slots.deliverable: A package with three sequential Execute SQL Tasks connected by precedence constraints, running end to end successfully, with the captured result-set value visible in a watch window during debug.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a small child package that processes one flat file, then build a parent package with a Foreach Loop Container (Foreach File Enumerator) that iterates over a folder of 3-5 sample CSV files, calling the child package once per file via an Execute Package Task with the file path passed through a mapped variable.
slots.deliverable: A working parent/child package pair where the Foreach Loop Container processes every file in the test folder, confirmed by logging or a breakpoint showing each filename handled by the Execute Package Task.

slots.practicalActivity: Refactor the three-task Execute SQL package from the earlier slot by grouping the tasks into a Sequence Container, then add a second Sequence Container with tasks connected by Success, Failure, and Completion precedence constraints, including at least one expression-based constraint.
slots.deliverable: An updated package with two Sequence Containers: one grouping the staging tasks, and one demonstrating all three precedence constraint types with an expression-based constraint, verified by forcing a failure and watching the correct branch execute.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Data Flow Task to a new package with an OLE DB Source reading from a source table and an OLE DB Destination writing into a new staging table, mapping columns manually to see the full source-to-destination pipeline in action.
slots.deliverable: A package with one Data Flow Task that moves rows from the source table into a new staging table, run successfully with row counts visible on the data flow path.

slots.practicalActivity: Re-run the previous slot's data flow against a larger source table and use the Execution Results tab to observe buffer counts and rows-per-buffer. Then switch the OLE DB Destination between Fast Load and table-or-view access mode and compare execution time between the two settings.
slots.deliverable: A short annotation on the package recording the buffer counts and execution-time difference observed between Fast Load and normal OLE DB Destination mode on the same source table.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Flat File Connection Manager and Flat File Source reading a sample CSV, route it to a Flat File Destination writing a transformed copy, and insert a Data Viewer (grid) on the path between them to pause execution and inspect rows mid-flow.
slots.deliverable: A package that reads a CSV through a Flat File Source and writes it to a new Flat File Destination, with the Data Viewer grid confirmed to pop up and display live row data during a debug run.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a data flow that reads order rows, uses a Lookup Transformation against a customer dimension table (configured to redirect rows to the no-match output), then feeds a Conditional Split that routes matched rows to one destination and unmatched rows to a separate exception staging table.
slots.deliverable: A package demonstrating a Lookup Transformation with configured no-match handling feeding a Conditional Split that separates matched from unmatched rows into two destination tables, verified by seeding a few rows with no matching customer.

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the previous slot's data flow with a Derived Column transformation that computes a new calculated column (e.g., ExtendedPrice = Quantity * UnitPrice), and a Data Conversion transformation that converts a string column to the correct numeric or date data type before loading.
slots.deliverable: The data flow now includes a Derived Column producing a correctly calculated column and a Data Conversion transformation that resolves a data type mismatch, confirmed by loading into a strongly-typed destination table with no truncation or conversion errors.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a data flow that uses an Aggregate transformation to compute SUM and COUNT grouped by a category column, then feeds the aggregated output through a Sort transformation before loading it into a summary table, matching the sort order a downstream Merge Join would require.
slots.deliverable: A package with an Aggregate transformation producing grouped totals and a Sort transformation ordering the output, loaded into a SummaryByCategory table and verified against a manual SQL GROUP BY query.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a data flow with two sorted OLE DB Sources (sort keys set in the Advanced Editor) feeding a Merge Join transformation configured as a Left Outer Join, combining order-header and order-detail data into one output stream loaded into a destination table.
slots.deliverable: A working Merge Join transformation combining two sorted sources into a single output, loaded into a destination table, with the row count verified against an equivalent T-SQL LEFT JOIN.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review lab for Data Flow Transformations: without new instruction, build one original package from scratch that chains at least four of this chapter's transformations together — e.g. Lookup -> Conditional Split -> Derived Column -> Aggregate (or Sort/Merge Join) — solving a single realistic ETL problem such as enriching order lines with customer region, flagging high-value orders, and summarizing revenue by region.
slots.deliverable: One original package combining at least four Data Flow Transformations chapter techniques into a single coherent, successfully executing pipeline, with a short annotation describing the business problem it solves.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a package-scoped variable holding a row-count threshold, a project parameter for a source folder path, and a package parameter for a target schema name. Build an Expression on a precedence constraint or Derived Column that references the variable and changes the package's behavior.
slots.deliverable: A package exposing one package variable, one project parameter, and one package parameter, all actively referenced by at least one expression, with behavior demonstrably changing when the variable/parameter value is changed and the package re-run.

slots.practicalActivity: Convert an OLE DB Connection Manager's connection string to use Expressions driven by project parameters (server name, database name), then test switching the package between two different target databases purely by changing parameter values at execution time, no redeploy.
slots.deliverable: A package whose Connection Manager connection string is fully parameter-driven, demonstrated by running it twice with different parameter values and confirming data lands in the correct target database each time.

lessons.title: Error Outputs on Data Flow Components

slots.practicalActivity: Add an OnError event handler at the package level that writes failure details to a logging table whenever any task fails, and configure the Error Output on a Data Flow Destination (or Lookup) from an earlier chapter's package to redirect bad rows into a dedicated error-rows table instead of failing the whole package.
slots.deliverable: A package where a deliberately broken connection string triggers the OnError event handler (logged to a table) and a deliberately malformed source row is redirected by the Error Output into an ErrorRows table, both proven in the same debug run.

slots.practicalActivity: Enable SSIS logging to a SQL Server log provider table capturing OnError and OnTaskFailed events for a multi-task package, then enable Checkpoints on that package and force a mid-package failure to confirm it restarts from the failed task on re-run rather than from the beginning.
slots.deliverable: Visible log rows in the chosen log table after a run, plus a demonstrated checkpoint restart: force a failure partway through, re-run, and confirm already-completed tasks are skipped.

slots.practicalActivity: Deliberately reproduce three common SSIS failure patterns from the lesson one at a time against a test package — e.g. a locked flat file, a truncated string column, and an expired or invalid connection string — and document the exact error message and fix for each.
slots.deliverable: A short troubleshooting log recording three deliberately reproduced failures, their exact SSIS error messages, and the specific fix applied to resolve each one.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review lab for Error Handling & Logging: build one small original package covering the chapter end to end — a multi-task control flow with checkpoints enabled, an OnError event handler, SQL Server logging turned on, and a data flow with error-output redirection — then deliberately trigger a failure to prove every layer activates correctly.
slots.deliverable: One original package demonstrating checkpoints, an event handler, logging, and error-output redirection working together, proven by a single deliberate-failure test run with log-table rows, error-row-table rows, and a confirmed restart-from-checkpoint.

slots.practicalActivity: Build an incremental-load pattern using a last-modified-date watermark stored in a control table to pull only new or changed source rows, then build a second data flow using the Slowly Changing Dimension transformation wizard against a dimension table to handle both a Type 1 attribute update and a Type 2 new-row insert.
slots.deliverable: Two working data flows: a watermark-based incremental load that pulls zero rows on a second run (verified by running it twice), and an SCD Transformation that correctly produces both a Type 1 update and a Type 2 insert on a changed attribute.

lessons.title: Script Tasks & Script Components: C# Basics

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Script Task that uses C# to check whether a source file exists before continuing the control flow, and a Script Component transformation that applies custom row-level logic (e.g., trimming/cleansing a string column) not available in a standard transformation. Then externalize key settings using a package configuration file.
slots.deliverable: A package with a working C# Script Task that branches based on file existence, a Script Component performing custom row logic in the data flow, and settings controlled via an external configuration file, demonstrated by changing the config and re-running without opening the package in SSDT.

slots.practicalActivity: Refactor several existing packages into a master/child pattern: create one Master.dtsx package that calls three earlier packages in sequence via Execute Package Task, passing a shared parameter (e.g., a BatchID) down into each child.
slots.deliverable: A Master.dtsx package that successfully orchestrates three existing child packages in sequence, passing a single shared BatchID parameter value into each and confirming it is used/logged consistently across all three.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter review lab for Advanced SSIS Patterns: build one original package combining at least three of this chapter's techniques — an incremental/watermark load, a Script Task or Script Component for custom logic, and a master/child call structure — into one realistic scenario, such as a nightly incremental customer-dimension refresh orchestrated from a master package.
slots.deliverable: One original package combining incremental loading, a Script Task/Component, and master/child orchestration into a single coherent, successfully executing nightly-refresh-style pipeline.

slots.practicalActivity: Deploy one of your existing projects to the SSIS Catalog (SSISDB) on your local SQL Server using the Integration Services Deployment Wizard, then create an Environment in the catalog with variables for the connection string and batch folder path, and map them to the deployed project's parameters.
slots.deliverable: A project visible in the SSIS Catalog under a folder, with one Environment created and its variables successfully mapped to the project's parameters, confirmed by a successful catalog-based execution using that environment.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a SQL Server Agent job with a step that executes the deployed catalog package using the Environment from the previous slot, schedule it to run daily, then manually start the job and use the SSIS Catalog's Standard Reports (All Executions) to review the run's status, duration, and messages.
slots.deliverable: A working SQL Server Agent job that successfully executes the deployed SSIS package against its environment, plus a reviewed All Executions report showing the completed run with its status and duration.

slots.practicalActivity: Define the capstone scope: pick a realistic source-to-target ETL scenario (e.g., loading sales data from flat files plus a source database into a small staging/mart schema), sketch the control flow and data flow, and list every connection manager, parameter, and table the build will need.
slots.deliverable: A one-page capstone plan listing the chosen scenario, a control-flow sketch, a data-flow sketch, and the full list of connection managers, parameters, and tables to be built in the following lab sessions.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone lab session 1: create the capstone project in SSDT, set up every Connection Manager and project/package parameter planned in the kickoff, and build the Control Flow skeleton (Execute SQL Tasks for staging truncation, Sequence Containers, and placeholder Data Flow Tasks).
slots.deliverable: A capstone project with all Connection Managers and parameters configured and a complete, runnable Control Flow skeleton (with empty Data Flow Task placeholders) that executes end to end without errors.

lessons.title: Capstone: Building a Real ETL Package

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone lab session 2: build out the real ETL Data Flow(s) inside the capstone package - Source components, at least one Lookup, a Conditional Split or Derived Column, and a Destination - fully loading the target staging/mart tables from the chosen source data.
slots.deliverable: A capstone package whose Data Flow Task(s) fully execute, loading real rows from source into the target mart/staging tables, verified by row counts matching the expected source row count.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone lab session 3: stress-test the capstone build by re-running it against modified source data - new rows, a changed attribute, and a deliberately bad row - to confirm the data flow handles each case correctly before adding incremental logic and error handling in the next session.
slots.deliverable: A written log of three test runs (new rows, changed attribute, bad row) against the capstone package noting the actual outcome of each, with any bugs found fixed directly in the package.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone lab session 4: add incremental-load logic (a watermark table or SCD Transformation, whichever fits the capstone scenario) plus full error handling - error-output redirection on the data flow, an OnError event handler, and logging to a log table - matching the standards built earlier in the course.
slots.deliverable: The capstone package now supports incremental runs (a second run loads only new/changed rows) and has error redirection, an event handler, and logging all active, verified by a deliberate bad-row test and a repeat-run test.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone lab session 5: deploy the finished capstone project to the SSIS Catalog, create an Environment with production-style parameter values, and schedule it via SQL Server Agent, then execute it end to end from the Agent job and confirm success in the catalog's execution reports.
slots.deliverable: The capstone project deployed to the SSIS Catalog with an Environment configured and a SQL Server Agent job that successfully triggers and completes a full catalog execution, confirmed in the All Executions report.

slots.practicalActivity: Prepare a short portfolio walkthrough of the finished capstone project: write a one-page README describing the scenario, architecture, and techniques used (control flow, transformations, incremental load, error handling, deployment), and rehearse a 3-5 minute demo of the package running in SSDT and in the catalog.
slots.deliverable: A completed capstone README/portfolio writeup plus a rehearsed end-to-end demo of the package executing successfully, ready to show in an interview or portfolio.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After completing this course, a student can design, build, debug, and deploy real-world ETL packages in SSIS/SSDT, including control flow orchestration, data flow transformations, incremental loads, error handling and logging, and SSIS Catalog deployment, culminating in a portfolio-ready capstone ETL project.
